system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}

CONCEPT: Group barrier

ATOM DPCPP2-C09-S2-01 (S2): The set of work-items that synchronize at a group_barrier is determined entirely by the group object passed to it, while the optional memory-scope argument only affects the memory operations performed by the barrier, so passing a different scope cannot synchronize more or fewer work-items.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0260-s05] Please note that the explicit scope only affects the memory operations
[DPCPP2-p0260-s06] that are performed by the barrier, and that the set of work-items that synchronize execution at the barrier is determined entirely by the group object passed to the barrier.
[DPCPP2-p0260-s07] We cannot synchronize more or fewer work-items by passing a different memory scope to the barrier, but we can synchronize a different set of work-items by passing a different group object to the barrier.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Split group-controlled execution participation from the memory-scope argument’s restriction to memory operations; these are independently assessable claims. / Combines two distinct claims: the group object determines synchronizing work-items, and the memory-scope argument only affects memory operations.
